physical_harm: Rape and threats causing physical and mental harm
number_of_offences: Two charges: 506(2) IPC initially, 376 IPC added later; both upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the fact that the charge under Section 376 IPC was added nine years after the initial charge under Section 506(2) IPC, and that the prosecutrix did not take any steps for almost 9 years. The Court also accepted that the investigation was complete and there was no allegation that the appellant may flee the course of justice.
witness_credibility: The Court assessed the main witnesses, including the prosecutrix, by noting that her statement recorded on 31.05.2001 did not contain allegations of rape, and that the statement was later supplemented by her complaint to Jyoti Sangh. The Court also noted that the prosecutrix did not object to the initial charge under Section 506(2) IPC and that there was no evidence of her trying to influence the witnesses.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant participated in the proceedings throughout the period and there is no allegation that he tried to influence the witnesses.
bail_history: Anticipatory bail granted by the Sessions Judge, cancelled by the High Court, restored by the Supreme Court
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 1997-98; Trial judgment: 2014; High Court decision: 18.07.2014; Supreme Court decision: 01.09.2015
legal_representation: For the accused: Dushyant Dave, Harin Raval, Anirudh Sharma, Samar Kachwaha, Nachiket Dave, Raghavendra M. Bajaj, Anando Mukherjee, Nipur Saxena, Praveen Kumar Hota; For the State: Hemantika Wahi, Jesal Wahi, Puja Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Anticipatory bail granted; High Court: Anticipatory bail cancelled; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, bail restored
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the addition of a serious charge under Section 376 IPC should disqualify the appellant from anticipatory bail, and that the delay in framing the charge and the prosecutrix's inaction were factors to consider.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the addition of the charge under Section 376 IPC after a long period and the prosecutrix's inaction were contributory factors, and that the appellant should not be denied anticipatory bail merely because of the serious charge.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the grant of anticipatory bail should not be denied merely because a serious charge is added later, and that the court must balance the interests of individual liberty and societal interest.
precedent_relied_upon: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 sec 565: 1980 (3) SCR 383; Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra and Others (2011) 1 SCC 694: 2010 (15) SCR 201
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court weighed the fact that the investigation was complete, the appellant had participated in proceedings, and there was no allegation of fleeing justice or influencing witnesses.
